sections.whatsHappening: You cannot bring a claim for these damages unless you give written notice of your claim to the municipality. You must serve this notice within 10 days after the occurrence of the injury.
sections.whatToDoNext: Prepare your written notice of the claim. Include details of the injury, the date, time, and location of the occurrence. Serve the notice upon or send it by registered mail to the clerk of the municipality.
sections.yourDeadline:
Give written notice of the claim to the clerk of the municipality. You have 10 days, counted from the occurrence of the injury.

This deadline is set by a statute rather than by the court's rules, and that changes how the days are counted. Under the rules a deadline landing on a Saturday moves to the next working day. Under the statute it does not — only Sunday and holidays are excluded. Do not assume a weekend gives you extra time.
sections.whatHappensAfter: If you do not give notice within the required time, you may not be able to bring your claim. However, failure to give notice is not a bar to the action if a judge finds there is a reasonable excuse for the lack of notice.
